daily.title: Iran: Exiled journalists still repressed by regime
daily.summary: For many independent reporters, leaving Iran does not mean fully escaping the grasp of the Iranian state. The regime uses family members, bank accounts and the property they left behind to apply pressure across borders.

daily.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns as scandal mounts over alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy
daily.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from his role as the head of the AI chipmaker over his reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia shares plummeted 13% at the opening of trading on Thursday.

daily.title: China's Xi Jinping renews calls for 'reunification' with Taiwan
daily.summary: Xi Jinping said that reunification was inevitable, but stopped short of mentioning military force. Taiwan though swiftly rejected Beijing's demands as tensions continue over the island's future.

daily.title: What are fossil fuels?
daily.summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

daily.title: Israel strikes Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure inside
daily.summary: Israel says Hamas was using the hospital as a military command center, while Palestinian officials report at least six people killed, including a surgeon. The strike comes amid an increasingly fragile ceasefire.

daily.title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
daily.summary: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes. Follow DW.

daily.title: Australian teen found alive after six days in the bush
daily.summary: The teenager was spotted during an aerial search, after spending days navigating rugged terrain. He had fallen down the side of a riverbed two days before being found.

daily.title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
daily.summary: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."

daily.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
daily.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

daily.title: India news : Modi government approves $340 million museum in Delhi
daily.summary: The government says that the 'Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum' will have the world's "largest" museum dispaly area." DW has the latest.

daily.title: Ukraine peace talks: US envoys meet with Putin at Kremlin
daily.summary: The US president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff are in Russia to meet Vladimir Putin. The meeting comes after two days of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: Where the US's war with Iran stands after the midterms
daily.summary: Almost nine months after it began, the war in Iran has calmed to the point where Donald Trump sees an end. But with the key issues of the conflict unresolved and political change in the US, what is the situation?

daily.title: Pope Leo XIV returns to Peru to a big welcome, calls it his 'homeland'
daily.summary: An estimated 3 million people greeted Pope Leo XIV in Lima as the Peruvian-citizen pontiff began a six-day homecoming visit to the country where he spent two decades as a missionary and bishop.

daily.title: Nvidia board reportedly weighs ousting Huang amid alleged affairs with exec and suspected Chinese spy
daily.summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang amid reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The shake-up would leave the world's leading AI chip supplier without the co-founder who built it.

daily.title: Mississippi Senate race: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith
daily.summary: The southern US state of Mississippi has elected its first Black senator in more than 140 years. Democrat Scott Colom has won the seat in a historic upset, according to projections.

daily.title: Russian Foreign Ministry says its ambassador to US has died
daily.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry has said that Alexander Darchiev died from a chronic illness at the age of 66. The long-time diplomat had been in the Washington post since early 2025.

daily.title: Spain: Housing crisis prompts general strike, mass nighttime protests
daily.summary: Hundreds of thousands of citizens have hit the streets to protest Spain's housing crisis after millions of union workers staged a general strike. The crisis has triggered snap elections to take place on November 29.

daily.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
daily.summary: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?

daily.title: VW scraps production modernization plan citing tough financial straits
daily.summary: VW has announced that it will scrap large-scale modernization in light of its current economic situation. Employee representatives accuse leadership of putting short-term profits before long-term company viability.

daily.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
daily.summary: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

daily.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
daily.summary: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

daily.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
daily.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

daily.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
daily.summary: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

weekly.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
weekly.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

weekly.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
weekly.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

weekly.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
weekly.summary: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

weekly.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
weekly.summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

weekly.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
weekly.summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

weekly.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
weekly.summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

weekly.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
weekly.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

weekly.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
weekly.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

weekly.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
weekly.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

weekly.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
weekly.summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

weekly.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
weekly.summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

weekly.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
weekly.summary: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

weekly.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
weekly.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

weekly.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
weekly.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

weekly.title: US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
weekly.summary: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

weekly.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
weekly.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

weekly.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
weekly.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

weekly.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
weekly.summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

weekly.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
weekly.summary: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

weekly.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
weekly.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

weekly.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
weekly.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

weekly.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president
weekly.summary: The steering committtee of the CDU have announced Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate. This gives her a good chance of becoming the first woman to occupy the role.

weekly.title: EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
weekly.summary: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

weekly.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
weekly.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

weekly.title: Who is Ilse Aigner, leading candidate for Germany's next president?
weekly.summary: She would be the first female president and the first Christian Social Union politician to hold Germany's highest office. Ilse Aigner is the favored candidate for the Federal Convention vote on January 30.

weekly.title: Germany news: Germany marks fateful date of November 9
weekly.summary: Germany is commemorating the Nazi-led November pogroms 88 years ago. Events are also being held to mark the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. DW has more.

weekly.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
weekly.summary: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

weekly.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
weekly.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

weekly.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
weekly.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

weekly.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
weekly.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

weekly.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
weekly.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

weekly.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
weekly.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

weekly.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
weekly.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

weekly.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
weekly.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
weekly.summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
weekly.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

weekly.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
weekly.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

weekly.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
weekly.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

weekly.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
weekly.summary: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

weekly.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
weekly.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

weekly.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
weekly.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

weekly.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
weekly.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

weekly.title: Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
weekly.summary: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

weekly.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
weekly.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?
